I should word this carefully to avoid just echoing the postmortem's phrasing like "back to normal" — better to describe the actual sequence of events factually: Argus flagged the HighErrorRate alert at 23:49, tracing back to the monthly-spend-feature flag being enabled at 23:43, which triggered a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py line 47.

The mitigation agent flipped the flag off at 23:49:06, and by 23:51:03 the service had recovered, confirming the incident as mitigated with no deployment involved. A Code-Fix Agent opened draft PR #370 for review but it hasn't been merged, and the postmortem flags that re-enabling the feature would likely reproduce the same failure, so the flag remains off for now.

input.answer:
Argus got a HighErrorRate alert on io-shop at 23:49 UTC and started investigating. It found that the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 23:43. That turned on code that raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the account page error rate went from about 1% to about 33%. No deployment had gone out, and latency and resources were flat.

At 23:49:06 Argus switched monthly-spend-feature from ON to OFF. When it checked at 23:51:03, the service was no longer at the incident's level, and had not been since 23:49. Argus confirmed that the flag change worked, marked the incident MITIGATED, and the flag is still off.

Argus has also opened a draft fix, PR #370 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/370), which needs someone to review and merge it, and it has written the postmortem. The postmortem warns that the faulty calculation is still in the code, so turning the flag back on would most likely make account pages fail again for shoppers who haven't bought anything this month.
